mustFixDetail.title: All four namedOpenDecisions standings are carried verbatim from the predecessor in the predecessor's voice, so the subject states no standing of its own on any of its own named open questions, and the bare token `golden.v3` resolves against two distinct golden lineages the subject itself pins.

mustFixDetail.measurement: All four strings are byte-identical to sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v3 (236fdb338d7bc441bf0315a3c7cc51580f83c20c2cbc3e1e945c742ed3b32179) namedOpenDecisions[0..3].standing, compared field by field. Not one character was changed when the array was carried into the successor. `namedOpenDecisions` carries no `quoted` prefix and no source attribution, unlike the four fields in this same document that are explicit quotations and are named as such — quotedD9Golden, quotedClassToExitCode, quotedV15OwnerOfValues, d002PlatformsQuotedFromG10OccupancyV2. It is presented as the subject's own field, so its speaker is sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v4, which the dispatch states in terms: "Speaker is sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v4."
mustFixDetail.whyItIsADefect: Two independent limbs, both new at v4. (1) Voice. At sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v3 the token `golden.v3` was the speaker naming itself, and dual ACCEPT 0/0 at D-297 graded it in that reading. At sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v4 the same token has no antecedent in the speaker, so the subject's four open-question standings state what a frozen predecessor did and never state what sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v4 does. The subject self-names 35 times elsewhere in the file, including inside purpose, authorityClaim, registerRowNote, remainderAfterThisCorpus, every basedOn role and all five proposedLaterWork members; namedOpenDecisions is the only block where the speaker is absent. (2) Ambiguity, and falsity under one resolution. `golden.v3` is unqualified, and the subject pins two distinct golden lineages each having a v3: sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v3 at basedOn.predecessorGoldenV3 and sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v3 at basedOn.nonauthGoldenV3. Resolved against the nonauth lineage, namedOpenDecisions[2] and [3] are false on live bytes — sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v3 authors two FC-NONAUTH-TERM refuse implementations and no serialization witness, and carries no `help` command witness. The subject's own doesNot even states "Does not author FC-NONAUTH-TERM", which is the collision this token invites. Every other version token in the file is lineage-qualified, and the dispatch's own attack list charges exactly this shape for the join lineage ("leftover-join.vN tokens not lineage-qualified").
mustFixDetail.refutation: Three defences were constructed and each fails on live bytes. (a) That the standings are historical notes about the predecessor and are correct as such. They are correct as such, which is why this is graded on the successor's silence rather than on falsity: an artifact whose whole act is a copy-act must say where it stands on the four questions it lists, and this one does not. namedOpenDecisions[2] is the sharp case — read as the subject's own standing it says the subject "authors one serialization witness", a first-authoring claim the subject elsewhere expressly disclaims (authorityClaim: "copies the D-297 no-committed-run implementation"; namedCases[1].firstAuthoringPath fixtures/sarif-fc-outfail.v1/, firstAuthoringRecording D-297); read as a note about v3 it leaves the subject's own standing unstated. There is no reading on which the field does its job. (b) That inheritance is settled practice because the strings survived dual ACCEPT at D-297. Argument from silence, and it is refuted by the record: at D-297 the strings were self-reference by the artifact named in them, so the finding could not have arisen there. (c) That copy-act successors in this corpus carry predecessor standings untouched. Refuted directly and decisively by the sibling the subject itself cites as governing. sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v4 (940c478add7be442531dc2d1b2dd447de0d5cd66cd83b8312b0c0a37412762e5, D-344, dual ACCEPT 0/0, cited at basedOn.goldenNonauthV4 as "Sibling copy-act" and named in authorityClaim as "sibling copy-act practice") inherited the identical construction from sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v3, whose three standings likewise read "golden.v3 uses…", "golden.v3 authors…", and rewrote every one of them to name the successor in full: "sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v4 uses only REQUEST.UNKNOWN_OPTION…", "sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v4 copies those two namedCases and no fifth case", "sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v4 uses one already-recorded projection surface (json)…". The sibling's second standing even uses the verb "copies" in place of the predecessor's "authors" — precisely the correction missing at namedOpenDecisions[2] here. The accepted practice for this exact act, in this exact corpus, one heading ago, is the opposite of what the subject did.
mustFixDetail.remedy: Re-voice all four standings to name sarif-fc-outfail-golden.v4 in full, following the accepted sibling form at sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v4. In particular, namedOpenDecisions[2] must describe the copy-act rather than a first authoring — the D-297 no-committed-run serialization witness is copied onto four D-002 platforms, not authored here. Nothing else in the file needs to change to fix this.

shouldFixDetail.measurement: The clause names fourteen files. Eleven are pinned somewhere in the subject and all eleven recompute exactly against live bytes. Three are pinned nowhere in the document at any depth: occupancy v2 of G26 (live 3a6f13799ef960170370a2a74930d62778a9671b2065ac3e83ca485c21721ffb), sarif leftover-join.v5 and sarif leftover-join.v6. A full walk of the subject for path+sha256 pairs returns 44 pairs and none of the three appears. D-226, the recording the registerRowNote attributes the G26 occupancy standing to, carries no basedOn entry and no commit pin either.
shouldFixDetail.whyItIsADefect: The clause is an operative instruction to the recorder and an attestation of what was unmoved at measurement. For these three files the attestation is unfalsifiable and the instruction is unexecutable: no baseline digest exists in the document against which "unmoved" could be checked or reproduced. This lands on a live standing claim the subject also makes about another lineage — that occupancy v2 remains the current G26 occupancy remasurement and occupancy v1 is not — carried with no pin behind it.
shouldFixDetail.refutation: Two defences were tested. (a) That the named list is an absolute construction rather than an exhaustive checklist, so an entry needs no pin — the reasoning a prior Claude 2 review used to refuse OBS-1 against sarif leftover-join.v10. That precedent is the inverse case and does not reach this one: there the file was omitted from the clause while being fully pinned in basedOn and recordedInputs, so a recorder could still check it; here the file is named in the clause and pinned nowhere, so a recorder cannot. The defect is named-but-unpinned, not pinned-but-unnamed. (b) That the claims themselves are traceable to pinned inputs, so no pin is needed. Partly true and it is why this is SHOULD-FIX and not MUST-FIX: the G26 currency claim is carried in pinned sarif leftover-join.v11 OBL-G26, and the v5/v6 "Findings land at leftover-join.v7 of sarif" landings are carried in pinned live COORD at D-345. But traceability of a claim is not a baseline for an unmoved-attestation, and the clause asks for the latter. The defence also fails against the subject's own cited practice: sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v4 (D-344, dual ACCEPT 0/0) carries a remeasurementClause of identical shape naming the same three files, and pins all three — harness.DR-G26.preview-analyze-sarif-not-advertised.preview.v2.json 3a6f1379…, sarif-leftover-join.v5.json and sarif-leftover-join.v6.json with both reviews each — plus a basedOn.occupancyG26V2 entry with reviews and a basedOn.d226 entry with commit 7d12d3c0c6a635354c9dba790ecc5f209fcaf4b1. The subject dropped three pins its own named precedent carried while carrying that precedent's clause text forward unchanged.
shouldFixDetail.remedy: Either pin the three files (basedOn entries and recordedInputs, as the sibling does) or drop them from remeasurementClause. Pinning is preferable, since registerRowNote already asserts a live standing about occupancy v2 of G26.
